key_insight: Patient clinical data predicted 30-day bloodstream-infection mortality well, while adding microbial genes and proteins provided little to no extra predictive value.
clinical_relevance: For risk stratification in bloodstream infection, the biggest gains likely come from patient-level EMR models rather than pathogen trait profiling alone.
method: Combined electronic medical records with microbial genomes and quantitative proteomes (>70,000 microbial features).
Compared mortality prediction performance with and without microbial features using machine-learning models.
evidence_signal: EMR-based models predicted 30-day mortality with AUC=0.83, and adding microbial genes/proteins did not improve performance.
watch_item: The findings suggest microbial traits may be cohort-linked rather than independently predictive, so results may not generalize equally across settings or populations.
paper_title: Microbial traits have minimal power for predicting death from bloodstream infection
